name: Frankie Reyes
life: “I still remember a reunion picture taken just before my bus arrived.” On Monday, near the market by Market Flats, Frankie often waits until the delivery baskets are stacked before going in.
voice: I took a call during the photograph. My friends left a space and took another after I came back.
appearance: Frankie has a straight nose and deep-set eyes. Look for short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is an unlined tan jacket with a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair. In conversation Frankie rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket.
personality: Frankie prefers exact instructions at work and pleasant surprises at home. The two standards occasionally collide, especially when a relative thinks dropping by counts as notice.
agenda: To get into the second group photograph.
family: Irene Baines is Frankie’s cousin. Frankie puts the kettle on. Irene chooses the music. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *The skipper goes ashore*, Irene says, “I served under the skipper. She kept steering with a broken heart after her wife's death, so stopping now is hers to choose.”
connections: Erin Parra. A late photograph adds the classmate identified from the old inhaler story.

reactions.situation: A classmate arrives at the reunion in uniform
reactions.response: Frankie welcomes the classmate before bringing up their working clothes.

reactions.situation: A traveler asks for the last seat at the bus stop
reactions.response: Frankie looks for a second safe place to sit and stays long enough for the waiting people to settle.
